title: Deterministic CUDA-graph replay for concurrent prefill + multi-stream decode
creator: Marco Chen
description: Background: We observe intermittent replay failures and non-deterministic outputs when using CUDA graph capture + multi-stream decode on recent GPUs. Failures surface as: (1) incorrect KV cache alignment after replay, (2) occasional OOMs during graph replay under high concurrent prefill load, and (3) subtle token-level divergence vs. non-captured baseline. Goal: Deliver a set of changes to make CUDA-graph capture and replay deterministic and robust for concurrent prefill + decode workloads without regressing latency/throughput targets. Constraints: Maintain backward-compatible runtime config flags; avoid solutions that require per-request serialization that hurts P99 latency at scale. This ticket focuses on capture stability, deterministic replay ordering, and correct KV cache/attention state mapping across streams.
acceptance_criteria: Replays of captured graphs produce identical logits/token sequences vs. reference (no-capture) for 1000 sampled prompts across models (7B, 13B) with 8k context at batch size 16.
No replay-induced OOMs observed in stress test (3 hosts, 4 streams per GPU, 24h soak).
End-to-end P99 decode latency does not increase by more than 10% compared to baseline for typical PL workloads.
Automated CI/golden tests added that detect misaligned KV offsets and divergence in at least two model families.
implementation_steps: Audit current capture boundaries: identify where prefill vs. decode kernels are captured across streams and mark non-idempotent kernels.
Introduce deterministic stream reservation system: ensure capture uses pinned stream indices with explicit stream-to-cache mapping.
Add explicit KV cache versioning metadata into graph replay path so replays validate expected offsets before execution.
Implement guarded replay: on mismatch between expected and observed cache shapes, fall back to non-captured execution and emit telemetry.
Optimize memory pinning order to avoid transient OOMs during simultaneous replays (tighten allocator reservations during capture/launch).
Add CI golden-run harness for capture vs. non-capture output equivalence and integrate into presubmit.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged opt-in in runtime-1.19, canary on 5% of traffic, expand to 25% after 48h if stable, full enable after 7d.
Post-rollout: monitor regressions and revert flag if >0.5% request divergence or >5 replay fallbacks per million requests.
risks: Fallback-to-no-capture path may increase cost if mismatches are frequent; need to keep visibility to track root cause.
Changes to stream assignment may interact with other runtimes (Dedicated autoscaler) causing unexpected contention.
Hard-to-reproduce divergence on rare model/quantization combos — requires broad test coverage across quant profiles.
